 Reigning champ Jeeno Thitikul tied for lead at LPGA’s Tour Championship
 Nov 19, 2026 | 4:34 PM 
 Two-time defending champion Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand shares the first-round lead at the CME Group Tour Championship following a 7-under-par 65 on Thursday in Naples, Fla.
 Thitikul sits atop the leaderboard with Australia’s Karis Davidson and South Korea’s A Lim Kim. They’re one stroke ahead of a nine-way tie at 6-under 66.
 World No. 1 Nelly Korda, seeking her second CME Globe season-long title, is not far off the pace after opening with a 4-under 68.
 A $4 million prize is on the line for the winner of the LPGA’s finale at Tiburon Golf Club, with 60 players qualified.
 Thitikul, a former World No. 1, birdied five holes in a row starting at No. 13 to finish her day with nine birdies and two bogeys. She hit 13 of 14 fairways in regulation and 16 of 18 greens.
 “Hopefully I am the best friend of this golf course, I guess,” said the 23-year-old. “This golf course might like me as a friend so much, and I do like her for sure.”
 Davidson, 28, squeaked into the field this week at No. 55 in the season-long points chase.
 That didn’t matter once she teed off. Davidson birdied the first four holes at Tiburon and wound up with seven birdies, no bogeys and a perfect 14 fairways in regulation.
 “I think it’s definitely playing long,” Davidson said, “so to get some good approach shots on the first few holes and get a really good visual on the putts and get off to that good start was really helpful.”
 Davidson’s only professional win came on the WPGA Tour of Australasia. A win this week would be by far the biggest moment of her career. It’s also her first time qualifying for the Tour Championship.
 Asked what she would do with a $4 million paycheck, Davidson quipped, “Maybe some more business-class flights. Better for my body.”
 Kim, best known for winning the 2020 U.S. Women’s Open, carded six birdies on the back nine Thursday, including the final three in a row.
 “I play six time from here, so course layout is very comfortable (for me) now,” Kim said. “Just last year my homework is green read, so I’m still work on green read from now. So today it was good.”
 The nine players one shot off the pace are Jenny Bae, Lauren Coughlin, Auston Kim, France’s Pauline Roussin-Bouchard, Japan’s Ayaka Furue, Englishwoman Charley Hull and Koreans Somi Lee, Hye-Jin Choi and Haeran Ryu.
